citing_sentences: 1), a causal lossless subband architecture for byte-level autoregressive language modeling.

abstract: Byte level language models avoid tokenizer dependence and provide universal coverage, but processing every byte at full resolution is expensive. We introduce DeepMem, a causal multiscale architecture that separates semantic compression from exact byte preservation. A learned invertible subband transform constructs a hierarchy of shorter sequences, while a lossless carrier and explicit detail sidebands preserve byte identity. Fast weight memory blocks operate along the encoder, with iterative shared state computation at the compressed bottleneck, while an attention based super resolution decoder restores byte resolution representations. DeepMem achieves stronger language modeling performance than a matched byte level Transformer on FineWeb-Edu and PG19, and obtains the best macro average performance across the evaluated FLORES languages. It also improves PIQA accuracy while remaining competitive on code modeling, multiple choice reasoning, and byte level corruption robustness. Bottleneck refinement requires approximately $7{,}600\times$ fewer counted FLOPs than equivalent full resolution reasoning, while maintaining competitive evaluation throughput.

sections.body: The introduction frames the problem: subword tokenizers add a fixed external bottleneck, while byte-level models avoid it but process many more positions. DeepMem keeps a learned semantic stream that is progressively shortened, plus a lossless carrier in which each byte is a fixed eight-dimensional bipolar vector, transformed by learned lifting steps into coarse carriers and explicit detail sidebands. The paper reports about 100 million parameters, FineWeb-Edu at 1.0134 bits per byte (BPB) versus 1.0457 for a matched Transformer, PG19 at 1.4402 versus 1.4635, and a FLORES macro-average of 1.9694 versus 2.0082.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Tokenizer-free byte models are costly at full resolution, so DeepMem compresses semantics while keeping an exact byte carrier.

sections.body: The carrier hierarchy uses predict and update steps whose inverse reconstructs the original byte carrier exactly in real arithmetic, with zero-initialized final projections. The semantic stream is not invertible; it is pooled from adjacent vectors and passed through causal memory blocks. Fast-weight blocks use a recurrence in which a gated outer-product state is written and read by queries, so state size does not grow with length. The decoder uses shifted parent proposals so that a left child at position 2j receives information only from parent j-1, and training minimizes next-byte negative log-likelihood, converted to bits per byte.
sections.heading: Method
sections.headline: The method pairs learned invertible lifting over a lossless carrier with causal fast-weight encoders and an attention-based super-resolution decoder.

sections.body: Models train from scratch on FineWeb-Edu as UTF-8 bytes for 50,000 optimizer steps, an effective batch of 524,288 bytes per step, about 26.2 billion byte presentations. Baselines are a flat Transformer, FastWeight, BLT and AU-Net, all trained under the same budget. The reference DeepMem uses hierarchy lengths from 2,048 down to 16 and two shared-state bottleneck iterations, with 100,158,582 trainable parameters. Evaluation covers bits per byte on FineWeb-Edu, PG19, Stack-smol and eight FLORES languages, zero-shot multiple-choice accuracy, and HellaSwag under perturbations, with throughput reported in bytes per second.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: All models use about 100 million parameters, a 2,048-byte context and three seeds, and are evaluated on several benchmarks.

sections.body: On FineWeb-Edu DeepMem reaches 1.0134 BPB against 1.0457 for the Transformer and 1.0187 for FastWeight; on PG19 it reaches 1.4402 against 1.4635. On Stack-smol the Transformer is best at 2.4474 BPB, while DeepMem scores 2.4854. The FLORES macro-average is 1.9694 against 2.0082 for the Transformer, and throughput averages 119,718 bytes per second against 147,023 for the Transformer. Multiple-choice mean accuracy is 37.76 and HellaSwag is 30.30. The variant without shared-state refinement is close on every metric.
sections.heading: Results
sections.headline: DeepMem reaches the lowest bits per byte on FineWeb-Edu, PG19 and the FLORES macro-average, but trails the Transformer on Stack-smol.

sections.body: The discussion attributes the gains to separating semantic abstraction from exact local information and to iterative refinement at the deepest bottleneck with shared parameters. The authors argue that delayed parent proposals keep future bytes out of the decoder. The stated limitations are that experiments cover only about 100M-parameter models and one training budget, that the model trails the Transformer on Stack-smol, that its measured throughput is lower than the Transformer's, and that invertibility holds only in real arithmetic, not in finite precision.
sections.heading: Discussion and Limitations
sections.headline: Causal synthesis and bottleneck refinement are presented as the design's main contributions, with limits to scale, code and precision.

sections.body: The conclusion summarizes the architecture: a FastWeight encoder over shorter sequences, a two-step shared-state refinement at the bottleneck, and an invertible carrier hierarchy with detail sidebands feeding a causal super-resolution decoder. It reports improvements on FineWeb-Edu, PG19 and multilingual BPB over a matched byte-level Transformer, along with multiple-choice accuracy and accuracy under byte-level perturbations. It gives the code repository URL as the release location.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: The conclusion states that lossless multiscale representations with shared-state refinement offer a practical alternative to flat byte processing.

sections.body: The ablation tables compare the full model with variants that lack shared-state refinement, carrier injection, or all-scale fusion, and an all-attention variant, with BPB, throughput, FLORES language results and HellaSwag accuracy under perturbations. The all-attention variant has FineWeb-Edu BPB of 1.0613 against 1.0145 for the no-shared-state variant. The authors note that the comparisons are single runs and are exploratory. A final section reports future-perturbation causality tests on a randomly initialized all-scale fusion configuration, with a maximum shared-prefix difference of 5.0664×10^-6 over all 2,048 cutoffs.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix contains ablations of attention, carrier injection, all-scale fusion and refinement, plus a causality verification.
